migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC migration program governance, inventory all cryptographic assets (EHR database encryption, TLS 1.2 ECDHE inter-hospital links, HSMs, endpoints), and classify data by confidentiality lifetime (50+ years for genomic records).
prerequisites: Access to EHR vendor cryptographic documentation
Access to Utimaco HSM configuration records

migration_steps.activity: Engage EHR vendor formally to obtain their PQC roadmap, certification timeline for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, and written confirmation of supported cryptographic configurations under their certification policy.
prerequisites: Defined vendor questionnaire and evidence requirements

migration_steps.activity: Engage Utimaco to obtain written commitment and evidence plan for FIPS 140-3 validated firmware supporting ML-KEM and ML-DSA, including certification scope and availability dates (claimed Q1 2027).

Conduct cryptographic risk assessment and data lifetime analysis to prioritize systems; identify non-EHR systems (e.g., backup infrastructure, internal PKI, VPN) that can be migrated independently of EHR vendor certification.
prerequisites: Step 2 and Step 3 vendor responses received

migration_steps.activity: Develop hybrid PQC migration architecture for non-EHR systems using ML-KEM for key establishment and ML-DSA for signatures, ensuring FIPS 140-3 validated modules are used; document interoperability and fallback requirements.
prerequisites: Confirmed availability of FIPS 140-3 validated PQC modules for non-EHR systems

migration_steps.activity: Procure and deploy FIPS 140-3 validated PQC-capable modules for non-EHR systems (e.g., load balancers, VPN gateways, internal PKI) where vendor support exists; schedule outside change freeze (avoid Dec 1–Jan 15).
Pilot hybrid PQC (ML-KEM for key establishment, ML-DSA for signatures) on non-production non-EHR systems; validate performance, interoperability, and FIPS 140-3 compliance.
Migrate non-EHR production systems to hybrid PQC where FIPS 140-3 validated modules are available and vendor support confirmed; update operational runbooks and monitoring.
Monitor EHR vendor certification progress for ML-KEM and ML-DSA; obtain written certification evidence and updated configuration guidance when available.

Upon EHR vendor certification of ML-KEM/ML-DSA and Utimaco FIPS 140-3 validated firmware availability (forecast Q1 2027), plan and execute EHR database encryption and inter-hospital TLS migration to hybrid PQC, respecting change freezes and downtime limits.
prerequisites: EHR vendor written certification of ML-KEM and ML-DSA
Utimaco FIPS 140-3 validated firmware with ML-KEM and ML-DSA available and deployed

blockers.blocker: EHR vendor has not certified ML-KEM or ML-DSA and prohibits custom cryptographic configurations.
blockers.reason: MediTrust cannot modify EHR cryptography without vendor certification; using uncertified algorithms would violate vendor policy and potentially void support.
blockers.resolution_required: EHR vendor must complete certification of ML-KEM and ML-DSA and provide written evidence (certification statement, configuration guide).

blockers.blocker: Utimaco HSM firmware supporting ML-KEM and ML-DSA is forecast for Q1 2027 but not currently available or FIPS 140-3 validated.
blockers.reason: FIPS 140-3 mandate requires validated modules; without validated HSM firmware, PQC algorithms cannot be used for key establishment or signatures in production.
blockers.resolution_required: Utimaco must deliver FIPS 140-3 validated firmware with ML-KEM and ML-DSA and provide validation certificate and release notes.

blockers.blocker: FIPS 140-3 validated modules for ML-KEM and ML-DSA are not yet available for all system components.
blockers.reason: Security policy mandates FIPS 140-3 validated modules for all cryptography; using non-validated implementations is prohibited.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain FIPS 140-3 validation certificates for all PQC modules (HSM, TLS libraries, database encryption) before production use.

blockers.blocker: Change freeze from December 1 to January 15 restricts production changes.
blockers.reason: Migration activities requiring production changes cannot be scheduled during this period.
blockers.resolution_required: Schedule all production changes outside the freeze window; obtain exception approval if emergency.

blockers.blocker: Budget of $500,000 may be insufficient for full EHR migration including HSM upgrades, vendor certification costs, and integration.
blockers.reason: Full PQC migration across 3 hospitals and 15 clinics with HSM upgrades and vendor certification may exceed budget.
blockers.resolution_required: Prioritize non-EHR systems within budget; seek additional funding for EHR migration phase or negotiate vendor costs.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Not certified for ML-KEM or ML-DSA; no committed timeline provided.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Written certification statement for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, updated configuration guide, and support policy allowing PQC algorithms.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Forecast Q1 2027 for ML-KEM and ML-DSA support; not currently available or FIPS 140-3 validated.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: FIPS 140-3 validation certificate for firmware with ML-KEM and ML-DSA, release notes, and availability confirmation.

algorithm_roles.ML-KEM: Post-quantum key establishment (key encapsulation) for TLS 1.3 and database encryption key exchange; replaces ECDHE for inter-hospital traffic and protects long-term confidentiality of genomic records.
algorithm_roles.ML-DSA: Post-quantum digital signatures for authentication, integrity, and non-repudiation of EHR data and firmware updates; replaces RSA/ECDSA signatures where applicable.

cost_assumptions.category: HSM firmware upgrade and FIPS 140-3 validation (Utimaco)
Non-EHR PQC module procurement and deployment

raw_response.confidence: Medium — Non-EHR migration steps are feasible within budget and timeline, but EHR migration is blocked by vendor certification and HSM firmware availability (forecast Q1 2027). Budget estimate assumes vendor certification costs are contained; actual costs may vary.
